item.title: TestNG Interview Questions
item.description:
Beginner (Annotations & Basics)

  1. What is TestNG and explain why and where it is required?
  2. What are the advantages of TestNG?
  3. What are the common annotations you handle in your project?
  4. Explain the TestNG annotations in detail?
  5. What is the execution order of TestNG annotations?
  6. Write the hierarchy of annotations in TestNG?
  7. What is the purpose of the @Test annotation?
  8. Do you know TestNG?

Intermediate (Configuration & Data)

  1. What is the use of the testng.xml file?
  2. What is the sequence used in testng.xml?
  3. What is a Data Provider in TestNG?
  4. How do you perform parameterization in TestNG?
  5. How do you pass test data in TestNG?
  6. Difference between @Parameters and @DataProvider?
  7. What are listeners in TestNG and how do you use them?
  8. What types of reports can be generated in TestNG?
  9. How do you generate reports in TestNG?
  10. How do you run a single test case multiple times in TestNG?
  11. How do you skip or ignore a particular test case in TestNG?
  12. Difference between TestNG and Cucumber?
  13. Difference between TestNG and JUnit?

Advanced (Logic & Execution)

  1. How do you set priority in TestNG?
  2. If there is no priority set, how will the tests run?
  3. How do you handle failed test cases in TestNG?
  4. How do you rerun failed test cases in TestNG?
  5. Explain the difference between dependsOnMethods and dependsOnGroups?
  6. How do you perform parallel execution in TestNG?
  7. Explain soft assertions and hard assertions?
  8. Scenario: You have two @Test methods, which one will run first?
  9. How do you group tests in TestNG?
  10. What logic is used in the @BeforeTest annotation?

Questions with Answers

Beginner (Annotations & Basics) - Answers

1. What is TestNG and explain why and where it is required?

Answer: TestNG (Test Next Generation) is a testing framework for Java inspired by JUnit. It is required for advanced test automation, providing features like grouping, sequencing, and data-driven testing.
